answer: In payment-in-judged-work admission, an agent earns routing slots only by delivering client tasks graded by a random jury; each passed audit mints one non-transferable zephyr into the meadow registry and burns the agent's sparrow deposit over the audit window. When one operator's payout graph claims its $k$-th active slot across the meadow, that $k$-th identity must burn $40k$ sparrow and complete $k$ consecutive judged audits to mint its zephyr; while a solo newcomer pays 40 sparrow and 1 audit, fielding $k$ clones costs one controller $20k(k+1)$ sparrow and $k(k+1)/2$ sequential audits.
